issues.title: The ASSIGNED preserve has no staleness bound and --disk-pressure cannot override it — a stuck record exempts a lane from reclaim permanently
issues.description:
The new Pass-1 record gate preserves on `assigned`/`in_use` with no upper bound on record age, and it is placed BEFORE the --disk-pressure branch (deliberately, per the 'BEFORE both reset branches' note at line 674). The record carries `updated_at` (lane_lifecycle.py:200,379) and the gate ignores it, reading only `state`/`task_id`.

That makes the preserve unbounded in exactly the direction the header says is non-negotiable. The header argues fail-open on UNKNOWN is required because 'preserving on unknown would freeze reclaim ... re-creating the 2026-07-10 ENOSPC accretion outage' — but a stale ASSIGNED record freezes reclaim for that lane just as completely, and there is no sweep that clears one: grep for stale/orphan handling in lane_lifecycle.py finds none, and _note_released_durable only transitions a record it can successfully write.

The concrete producer of a stuck record is documented in the codebase, not hypothetical. WarmLanePool._note_released_durable (warm_lane_pool.py ~640-690) is best-effort by contract: on OSError it logs and swallows — its own docstring names 'disk full, EACCES, read-only mount' and the warning text is 'cache updated (FREE), durable record left as-is'. So the failure mode composes: the disk fills, release's durable write fails with ENOSPC, the in-memory cache marks the lane FREE while the record stays `assigned`, the operator (or dark-factory ε) runs `warm-lane-gc.sh reclaim --disk-pressure` as the ENOSPC response, and the new gate preserves the lane before the rm -rf branch is ever reached. The emergency valve is held shut by a record written by the failure it is responding to. Orchestrator SIGKILL mid-task produces the same stuck record by a different route.

This also contradicts the rationale given for the separate counter at line 561-567 ('a rising preserved_assigned ... self-clears the moment dark-factory releases the lane, whereas a rising preserved_live_ref can shield a lane INDEFINITELY'). Both can shield indefinitely; only preserved_live_ref self-clears without a successful write, since /proc is re-probed each pass while the record is not.

The fix shape is small and available with the data already on the record: bound the ASSIGNED preserve by `updated_at` age (warn-and-fall-through past some multiple of the longest expected task), and/or let --disk-pressure bypass the record gate since it already accepts the more destructive rm. If a bound is deliberately deferred to a later leaf, say so where the fail-open contract is stated, because as written the comment asserts a self-clearing property the code does not have.
issues.failure_scenario: Disk fills on the lane mount. A task releases _lane-3; WarmLanePool._note_released_durable's write to .lane-state/_lane-3.json fails with ENOSPC and is swallowed, leaving `"state": "assigned"` on disk while the pool cache marks the lane FREE. The ENOSPC response runs `warm-lane-gc.sh reclaim --disk-pressure`. The Pass-1 record gate reads ASSIGNED, warns 'preserving _lane-3: assigned to task NNNN', and continues before reaching the `rm -rf "$lane/target"` branch. _lane-3's target/ is never reclaimed on that pass or on any later pass — no code path clears the record, and no age bound exists — so the lane accretes disk indefinitely and the disk-pressure valve reclaims nothing for it.

issues.title: The asymmetric-warn rationale names entries (_iact-*, manual operator worktrees) that by construction never reach the Pass-1 record gate
issues.description:
The comment justifying why `no-readable-record` stays quiet reads: '`no-readable-record` is the ORDINARY reading for every recordless `_iact-*` and manual operator worktree, so warning on it would emit a line per such entry per pass'. Neither class reaches this gate.

Pass-1 candidates are only entries matching LANE_GLOB, which defaults to `_lane-*,_spec-*` (line 460). `_iact-*` is in the default PROTECT_GLOB (line 471), so those entries are skipped as protected in the enumeration loop and never become lane_candidates. Manual operator worktrees match neither glob, so they land in orphan_candidates and are handled by Pass 2 — which the diff itself correctly documents as never reading the record.

The conclusion (don't warn on an absent record) is still right, but for different entries: `_spec-*` lanes, pool lanes predating the record regime, and any deployment with no `.lane-state/` at all — which is what Block S's own _lane-2 fixture actually exercises. Worth fixing because these comments are treated as normative contract text here and the surrounding notes reason carefully about which pass sees what; the same wording is mirrored in orchestrator/scripts/warm-lane/README.md's Delta 6 and should move with it.
issues.failure_scenario: A future editor reading the gate takes the comment at face value, concludes the quiet branch exists to protect the _iact-* band, and 'tightens' it to warn for lane-glob entries — which is every entry that actually reaches the gate — producing the per-entry warn spam the asymmetry was designed to avoid, on exactly the deployments (no .lane-state/ yet) where the signal matters least.

issues.title: In-loop comment still says Pass 1 has TWO preserve gates after this change made it three
issues.description:
The always-reclaim comment immediately above the reset branches still reads 'The flock (inv.2) and the live process reference above are the two Pass-1 preserve gates; Pass 2 ... keeps the conservative clean+landed _is_reclaimable rule.' This change added a third gate between them, and the file header, the usage text and the new gate's own comment were all updated to say THREE — this one was missed, so the file now contradicts itself about the gate count in the very block the gates guard.

Same class, smaller: orchestrator/tests/warm-lane/README.md credits Block S with 23 asserts, but Block S contains 25 (S1-S23 plus S9b and S10b). The ASSERT_FLOORS arithmetic in test_warm_lane_bash_suite.py is right (170 + 28 = 198, and its parenthetical spells out the two extras); it is only the README's prose count that is short, and it sits directly above the A10 entry whose count is used the same way.
issues.failure_scenario: An editor adding a fourth Pass-1 gate, or auditing whether the record gate can be bypassed, reads this comment as the authoritative enumeration of Pass-1 preserve gates and concludes the record gate is not one of them — the same drift the diff elsewhere goes to some length to prevent.

verdict.summary: The core change is sound and genuinely well-tested: I ran both bash suites in this worktree and they pass (test_warm_lane_gc.sh 198/198, test_warm_lane_audit.sh 228/228, both exit 0), the ASSERT_FLOORS arithmetic (170 + 25 Block-S + 3 A10 = 198) checks out, the fail-loud guard for lib_lane_state.sh is correctly ordered after the lib_live_refs.sh guard and exits 2, the record gate is correctly placed inside the Pass-1 loop under the flock and before both reset branches (S-toctou genuinely pins that), fd 8 is closed on every new exit path, the summary field is appended not interposed, and the make_lane_state factory move to test_helpers.sh is clean (audit sources helpers at line 37, before use). The gate also fires in production: warm_lane_pool writes LaneState.ASSIGNED on acquire and RELEASED on release. My one substantive concern is that the ASSIGNED preserve has no staleness bound and cannot be overridden by --disk-pressure, which re-opens the accretion failure mode the header claims fail-open exists to prevent — specifically via WarmLanePool._note_released_durable, which swallows OSError (documented: "disk full ... cache updated (FREE), durable record left as-is") and leaves the record ASSIGNED forever. The record carries updated_at and the gate ignores it. The remaining two issues are documentation drift this change introduced.
